City Council of Monterey Park
  The City Council Acting on Behalf of the Successor Agency of the Former Redevelopment
 Agency, the Housing Authority, the Monterey Park Financing Authority and the Monterey Park
  Geologic Hazard Abatement District Agenda

  Regular Meeting
  Monterey Park City Hall Council Chambers
  320 West Newmark Avenue, Monterey Park, CA 91754

  Wednesday, November 5, 2025
  6:30 PM
  Mission Statement
The mission of the City of Monterey Park is to provide excellent service, foster growth and opportunity,
  and create a joyous and collaborative environment.
  Land Acknowledgment
We would like to acknowledge that the land we inhabit today was once known as Tovangaar, the home
 of the Gabrieleño-Tongva people. We show our respect to the Gabrieleño-Tongva people, as well as
  all Indigenous people, past, present, and future, and honor their labor as original caretakers of this
land. We commit to uplifting the Gabrieleño-Tongva people, invite you to acknowledge the history, and
  join us in caring for this land.

General Information
Documents related to an Agenda item are available to the public in the City Clerk’s Office located at
320 West Newmark Avenue, Monterey Park, CA 91754, during normal business hours and
at www.montereypark.ca.gov/agendas.

The public may watch the meeting live on the city’s cable channel MPKTV (AT&T U-verse, channel 99
or Charter Communications, channel 182) or by visiting the city’s website
at http://www.montereypark.ca.gov/133/City-Council-Meeting-Videos. Per the Americans with
Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in this meeting, please call City Hall at
(626) 307-1359 for reasonable accommodation at least 24 hours before a meeting. Council Chambers
are wheelchair accessible.

Public Participation
You may speak up to 5 minutes on an/each Agenda item and 5 minutes total for Consent Calendar.
 The Mayor and City Council may change the amount of time allowed for speakers. Written
Communication will be accepted up to 24 hours before the meeting by completing an online form
at www.montereypark.ca.gov/writtencomm.

While all comments are welcome, the Brown Act does not allow the City Council to take action on any
item not on the agenda. The Council may briefly respond to comments after Public Communications is
closed. Persons may, in addition to any other matter within the City Council's subject-matter
 jurisdiction, comment on Agenda Items at this time. If you provide public comment on a specific
Agenda item at this time, however, you cannot later provide comments at the time the Agenda Item is
considered.

The City Council, the Financing Authority (MPFA), the Housing Authority (MPHA), the Geologic
Hazard Abatement District (GHAD), and the Successor Agency (SA) of the City of Monterey
Park held a Regular Meeting of the Council in the Council Chamber, located at 320 West
Newmark Avenue in the City of Monterey Park, Wednesday, November 5, 2025, at 6:30 p.m.

  Communications and requested the addition of Public Works in Staff Communications to
  be heard before Finance.

5.  Public Communications

  • Joseph Leon, representing the San Gabriel Valley Mosquito & Vector Control
  District, thanked the City Council for his reappointment as a member to the Board.
  He provided tips to residents on how to prevent and report sightings of mosquitoes
  and shared his experience in advocating for the month of "Movember."

  • Mike Sonksen commented on an article in the Cascades Newspaper about the
  Barnes Park Pool Revitalization Community Engagement meetings and advocated
  his approval of the matter.

  • Veronica Prado articulated her lifelong experience with the Barnes Park Pool and
  its vital importance to the community.

  • Cindy Yee commented on her granddaughter's performance as the Civic Superstar
  during the Pledge of Allegiance, expressed her dedication to rebuilding the Barnes
  Park pool and shared her opinion on the City's alleged use of funds on certain
  projects in the City.

  • Margaret Leung spoke about the history of the Scudder family's potato chip factory
  in Monterey Park, mentioned the disappearance of the family's dedication plaque
  and urged the City to locate its whereabouts. She provided information about the
  San Gabriel Valley Power Up Beacon's (SGVPUB) petition to save the Barnes
  Park pool and encouraged residents to participate.

  • Edlyn Takahashi talked about her experience as the President and Board Member
  of the Mark Keppel High Aquatics Booster Club and relayed a comment she made
  ten years ago regarding an opportunity to rebuild the pool. She discussed the
  benefits of training in an Olympic-sized pool and articulated SGVPUB's goal to
  rebuild the pool.

6.  Staff Communications
  This item was heard after Agenda Item No. 9.G.
   73-336
  November 5, 2025

6.A. Public Works
  This Agenda Item was added during Agenda Revisions and Additions.

  Public Works Director Igoe exhibited a PowerPoint presentation notifying the
  public of the dates and locations for Garvey Improvements Projects meetings
  and the monthly compost giveaways.

6.B. Finance
  Director of Finance Garcia presented a PowerPoint presentation informing the public
  about the Housing Rights Workshops scheduled for the new fiscal year.

6.C. Recreation & Community Services Department
  Director of Recreation and Community Services Aguirre gave a PowerPoint
  presentation thanking the community for a successful Monster Mash event and for
  participating in the Dia de Los Muertos altar at the Langley Center. He introduced the
  dates for the Barnes Park Pool Revitalization Community Engagement Meetings and
  the Pictures at the Mural program, an opportunity to take images behind the
  Monterey Park mural and receive a free postcard.

  Recreation and Community Services Program Coordinator Sauza presented
  upcoming events at the Langley Center, which include the California Science Center
  Field Trip, the Mahjong Underground Intergenerational Mahjong Series and the
  Thanksgiving Lunch in partnership with the Young Women's Christian Association.
  She mentioned upcoming programs, which include Game Day Tuesday, a dream
  catcher creation workshop, events celebrating Native American Heritage Month at
  Barnes Park, an opportunity to honor the veterans at the American Legion Post 397,
  the Letters to Santa program, the Holiday Snow Village event, Santa's Jolly Journey
  and the 2026 Lunar New Year Festival.

  Director of Recreation and Community Services Aguirre along with the City Council,
  introduced Eagle Scout Award recipient Brandon Chao and presented him with a
  certificate for his achievement. Brandon depicted details about his Eagle Scout
  Project, the refurbishment of the Barnes Park sign and thanked his project coach and
  scout members for their support throughout the project.

6.D. Library
  Library Manager Vera provided a PowerPoint presentation with a recap of the events
  that occurred in the month of October, announced available media streaming and
  books to the public in celebration of Native American History Month and shared
  upcoming programming for the month of November which include, Dinovember Party,
  the In-N-Out Reading Program, the Coloring Club, the Teen Entrepreneurs Program,
  the Jr. Friendsgiving event, the Cards for Veterans workshop, the Poetry Reading
  and Writing workshop, a Legal Clinic, the Boba Generations event and announced
  the upcoming winter session of the Literacy For All Monterey Park program.

6.E. Police
  Police Chief Wiese shared a PowerPoint presentation informing the residents about
  the implementation of Assembly Bill 413, and their timeline to begin its enforcement.
  He introduced the department's brand-new patch campaign to represent Memorial
  and Veterans Day and the new application to reunite lost pets with their owners.
   73-337
  November 5, 2025

  Animal Services Supervisor Estrada, alongside Animal Services Officer Rodriguez,
  elaborated on the application's purpose and functionality to reunite lost pets to their
  owners. Records Supervisor Martinez exhibited a live demonstration on how to report
  and search for lost pets.

9.C. Purchase of Laptops and Desktop Computers for the Police Department
  The Chief of Police (“Chief”) requests authorization to replace the Police
  Department’s (“Department”) end-of-life laptops and desktop computers. Current
  laptops and desktops are out of warranty, no longer serviceable, and not compliant
  with Criminal Justice Information Services (“CJIS”) security requirements. Old laptops
  and desktops often lead to slow computer performance, system crashes, and are
  open to vulnerabilities.

  The Chief is requesting authorization for the IT Division to purchase 50 Panasonic
  laptops, 90 Dell desktop computers, and associated technology upgrades and
  accessories for a total amount not to exceed $400,000.

  Recommendation:
  It is recommended that the City Council consider:

  1. Waiving bidding requirements pursuant to Monterey Park Municipal Code §§
  3.20.050(2)(4) and authorizing the City Manager, or designee, to enter into an
  agreement with Dell Marking LP and Panasonic Connect North America
  Professional Services, LLC, in a form approved by the City Attorney, for
  desktop and laptop computers; and
  2. Take such additional, related action that may be desirable.

  Action Taken: The City Council approved the recommendation, on Consent
  Calendar.

9.D. Consideration and possible action to read by title only, waive further reading,
  and introduce Ordinance amending Titles 16 and 17 of the Monterey Park
  Municipal Code by adopting the 2025 Edition of the California Building
  Standards Code and the Monterey Park Amendments to the California Building
  Standards Code; set public hearing for December 3, 2025
  Every three years California adopts updated building standards codified in Title 24 of
  the California Code of Regulations. The draft ordinance (Attachment 1 to the staff
  report) incorporates the 2025 codes by reference and includes limited local
  amendments based on documented climatic, geological, and topographic conditions
  and administrative needs. This cycle primarily clarifies existing requirements and
  updates numbering, with targeted fire and life safety provisions. The staff report also
  explains how the ordinance complies with AB 130 by limiting local changes that are
  applicable to residential units to the narrow exceptions allowed by state law, and by
  treating other changes as administrative or fire authority supported.
   73-339
  November 5, 2025

Type Of Action: (Legislative)

The recommended action is to amend Monterey Park Municipal Code (MPMC) Titles
16 and 17 by adopting the 2025 Edition of the California Building Standards Code
(CBSC). In considering such action, the City Council acts in its discretionary
legislative capacity (formulating rules that apply to all future cases). For the proposed
amendments, the City Council must find that they are reasonably necessary because
of local climatic, geological or topographical conditions (Health and Safety Code §
17958.7). These findings, and the facts upon which they rely, are included within the
draft Ordinance (Attachment 1 to the staff report). Accordingly, a Notice of Exemption
has been prepared for the proposed ordinance (Attachment 2 to the staff report).

CEQA (California Environmental Quality Act):
Pursuant to the California Environmental Quality Act (“CEQA”) and the CEQA
Guidelines, the proposed Ordinance affects commercial development or businesses
and is not subject to further review under CEQA for the following reasons: (1) the
Ordinance is an action being taken for enhanced environmental protection (14 Cal.
Code Regs. § 15308); (2) there is no possibility that the ordinance may have a
significant effect on the environment (14 Cal. Code Regs. § 15061(b)(3)); and (3) it
will not result in a direct or reasonably foreseeable indirect physical change in the
environment (14 Cal. Code Regs. § 15060(c)(2)).

Recommendation:
It is recommended that the City Council consider:

  1. Reading by title only, waiving further reading, and introducing the proposed
  Ordinance;
  2. Scheduling a public hearing on December 3, 2025, for the second reading
  and adoption of the Ordinance; and/or
  3. Taking such additional, related, action that may be desirable.

Action Taken: The City Council approved the recommendation and introduced and
waived the first reading of the proposed Ordinance, on Consent Calendar.

Ordinance, 1st reading
An Ordinance adopting the 2025 Editions of the California Building Code, the
California Residential Code, the California Electrical Code, the California Mechanical
Code, the California Plumbing Code, the California Energy Code, California Wildland-
Urban Interface Code, the California Historical Code, the California Fire Code, the
California Existing Building Code, the California Green Building Standards Code, the
California Referenced Standards Code, the California Building Standards
Administrative Code, making certain amendments based upon local conditions; and
amending the Monterey Park Municipal Code to reflect such changes
   73-340
  November 5, 2025

9.E. Agreement with San Gabriel Basin Water Quality Authority for the Operation of
  the South El Monte Operable Unit (SEMOU) Treatment Facility
  Under an agreement with the San Gabriel Basin Water Quality Authority (WQA), the
  City of Monterey Park has been receiving reimbursement for costs related to the
  treatment of water contaminated by industrial activities from the 1940’s. The
  contaminated aquifer is located in an area called the South El Monte Operating Unit
  (SEMOU) that had been managed by the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA).

  On September 1, 2024, the California Department of Toxic Substances Control
  (DTSC) took over the management of the SEMOU, including the transfer of all
  responsibility from EPA to DTSC. The City’s agreement with WQA expired on August
  31, 2024. To continue receiving reimbursement for treatment costs (now through
  DTSC), the City would need to enter into a new agreement with WQA.

  Recommendation:
  It is recommended that the City Council consider:

  1. Authorizing the City Manager to execute the Agreement with the San Gabriel
  Basin Water Quality Authority (WQA), in a form approved by the City
  Attorney, for the operation of the South El Monte Operable Unit (SEMOU)
  Treatment Facility;
  2. Taking such additional, related, action that may be desirable.

  Action Taken: The City Council approved the recommendation, on Consent
  Calendar.

  9.I. Movember Awareness Month
  The Movember Foundation is the leading global organization dedicated to
  transforming men’s health. Since its inception, the Movember community has raised
  $1.3 billion and funded over 1,320 programs in 20 countries
  (https://us.movember.com/). These initiatives are saving and improving lives of men
  affected by prostate cancer, testicular cancer, and mental health programs.
  Each year, the Foundation challenges men to grow mustaches during Movember
  (formerly known as November) to spark conversations and raise critical funds for its
  men’s health programs.

  The mustaches serve as a symbol of awareness, encouraging men to prioritize
  annual checkups for prostate and testicular health. As a mustache grows, it becomes
  a conversation starter, spreading awareness and educating communities about the
  health issues men face. The Vision of the Movember Foundation is to create a lasting
  impact on the face of men’s health worldwide.

  Recommendation:
  It is recommended that the City Council consider:

  1. Adopting a Resolution declaring the month of November 2025 as
  “Movember”; and
  2. Taking such additional, related, action that may be desirable.

  Action Taken: The City Council approved Resolution No. 2025-R96, on Consent
  Calendar.

  associated charities

11. New Business

  11.A. Adopt a Resolution to Cast Votes for a City Member to the San Gabriel Basin
  Water Quality Authority Board
  The San Gabriel Basin Water Quality Authority ("SGBWQA") was established by the
  State Legislature under Senate Bill 1679 in 1992 to develop, finance, and implement
  groundwater treatment programs in the San Gabriel Valley. The SGBWQA is under
  the direction and leadership of a 7-member board consisting of the following: one
  member of each of the three overlying municipal water districts, one from a city with
  prescriptive water pumping rights, one from a city without prescriptive water pumping
  rights, and two representing water producers in the San Gabriel Basin.

  According to the bylaws of the SGBWQA, a city with prescriptive water pumping
  rights, of which Monterey Park falls under, may nominate and elect a City Member to
  the Water Quality Authority Board. All votes cast must be for only one candidate.

  Each City with pumping rights has one vote for each 10,000 residents or the majority
  thereof, as determined by the U.S. Census Data. The City of Monterey Park has six
  votes to be cast.

  This election is to fill the vacancy of the Board Member representing cities with
  pumping rights. The election will take place at the SGBWQA's regular meeting on
  Wednesday, December 17, 2025.

  Recommendation:
  It is recommended that the City Council consider:

  1. Adopting a resolution voting for a City Member to represent cities with
  prescriptive pumping rights on the Board of the San Gabriel Basin Water
  Quality Authority;
  2. Directing the City Clerk to send a copy of the Resolution to the San Gabriel
  Basin Water Quality Authority to receive no later than December 16, 2025, at
  12:00 p.m.;
  3. Taking such additional, related, action that may be desirable.

  Discussion: Assistant City Manager Garcia showed a staff report detailing the
  process of electing a City Member for The San Gabriel Basin Water Quality
  Authority.

  Action Taken: The City Council approved the recommendation, approved
  Resolution No. 2025-R97, and appointed Robert Gonzales, City of Azusa Mayor as
  the representative of the Board of the San Gabriel Basin Water Quality Authority.
   73-344
  November 5, 2025
